title: Move 37 and the chain of thought

questions.prompt: Which part of AlphaGo found Move 37?
feedback: The policy supplied intuition, but search made the selection. Both mattered.
Search chose the move, but it worked with policy and value networks. Both mattered.
Both: the policy estimated a 1 in 10,000 human-play chance; search still chose the move.

questions.prompt: Is a chain of thought a search?
feedback: Partly: a written chain can change course, but that does not guarantee a check of each step.
It can revise and be sampled many times, so “partly” is the useful distinction here.
Partly: revision and repeated sampling are possible; checking each step is not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: When Claude 3.7 Sonnet used a hint it was given, how often did its reasoning say so?
feedback: Chen et al. (2025) found about 25% on average when the hint was used, not 90%.
The reported average was about 25%, not 50%, conditional on using the hint.
About 25% on average, when the hint was used (Chen et al., 2025).

questions.prompt: What would make a chain of thought trustworthy?
choices: A record you can check, and checking it
feedback: More time alone does not guarantee a faithful, checked record.
A checkable record plus actual checking offers an operational basis for trust. The broader question remains open.
Size alone does not guarantee a faithful, checked record.
